title: Triangles and Quadrilaterals: Properties and Angle Sums
seo_title: Grade 7 Triangles and Quadrilaterals Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Describe, sort, define and compare triangles in terms of their sides and angles (equilateral, isosceles, right-angled, scalene); describe, sort, define and compare quadrilaterals in terms of length of sides, parallel and perpendicular sides, and size of angles (parallelogram, rectangle, square, rhombus, trapezium, kite); solve geometric problems using the angle sums.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 7 worksheets: kinds of triangles and quadrilaterals, angle sums of triangles and quadrilaterals, and shape problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: A square is a special rectangle.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
  • The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°.
  • An isosceles triangle has two equal sides and two equal base angles. An equilateral triangle has three angles of 60°.
  • A square is a special rectangle, rhombus and parallelogram.

Examples

Example

An isosceles triangle with top angle 40°

180 − 40 = 140

140 ÷ 2

Answer: base angles 70° each

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
360° in a triangleA triangle is 180°.
Base anglesIn an isosceles triangle they are equal.
A square is a rectangleIt has four right angles.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 7 say about 2-D shapes?
faq.a: Describe, sort, define and compare triangles by their sides and angles, and quadrilaterals by their sides, angles, parallel and perpendicular sides.

faq.q: Can a triangle have two right angles?

faq.a: A quadrilateral with two pairs of equal adjacent sides.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides. Use the tick marks.
items.e: All 3 sides are equal, so it is an equilateral triangle. The tick marks show 3 equal sides. Pointing down does not change the name.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides. Use the tick marks.
items.e: Exactly 2 sides are equal, so it is an isosceles triangle. The 2 slanted sides have tick marks, and the base has none.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides. Use the tick marks.
items.e: Exactly 2 sides are equal, so it is an isosceles triangle. An isosceles triangle can point down. Turning a triangle never changes its name.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides. Use the tick marks.
items.e: Exactly 2 sides are equal, so it is an isosceles triangle. It lies on its side, but 2 sides still have tick marks. An isosceles triangle can point in any direction.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides.
items.e: Exactly 2 sides are equal, so it is an isosceles triangle. Two sides are 6 cm, so exactly 2 sides are equal. The equal sides do not have to be the slanted ones.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its angles.
items.e: One angle is more than 90°, so it is an obtuse triangle. 100° is more than 90°. It has 2 acute angles too, but a triangle is named by its largest angle.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its angles.
items.e: All 3 angles are less than 90°, so it is an acute triangle. 60°, 50° and 70° are all less than 90°.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its angles.
items.e: One angle is exactly 90°, so it is a right triangle. The small square shows a 90° angle. The other two angles, 40° and 50°, are acute.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its angles.
items.e: One angle is more than 90°, so it is an obtuse triangle. 110° is more than 90°. Pointing down does not change the name.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its angles.
items.e: All 3 angles are less than 90°, so it is an acute triangle. 75°, 60° and 45° are all less than 90°.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its angles.
items.e: One angle is exactly 90°, so it is a right triangle. The small square shows a 90° angle. The triangle is turned, but it is still a right triangle.

items.q: Which triangle is a right triangle?
items.e: Triangle C has a small square in one corner, so one angle is 90°. It is turned, but it is still a right triangle.

items.q: Which triangle is obtuse?
items.e: Triangle A has one wide angle, more than 90°. The right triangle has a 90° angle, and the other two have only acute angles.

items.q: A triangle has angles of 90°, 45° and 45°. Classify it by its angles.
items.e: One angle is exactly 90°, so it is a right triangle.

items.q: A triangle has angles of 100°, 40° and 40°. Classify it by its angles.
items.e: 100° is more than 90°, so it is obtuse. Two acute angles do not make it acute: every triangle has at least 2.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle. Only opposite sides are equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides. Its angles, in order, are 60°, 120°, 60° and 120°. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides make it a rhombus. The angles are not 90°, so it is not a square.

items.q: A rectangle has all 4 sides 12 cm long. What is its best name?
items.e: It has 4 right angles (it is a rectangle) and 4 equal sides. That makes it a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle. Only opposite sides are equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. There are no right angles, so it is not a square.

items.q: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is it called?
items.e: Exactly one pair of parallel sides makes a trapezium. Parallelograms and rhombuses have 2 pairs.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram. There are no right angles and the sides are not all equal, so it is not a rectangle or a rhombus.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram. There are no right angles and the sides are not all equal, so it is not a rectangle or a rhombus. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 2 pairs of equal sides, and each pair is next to each other (not opposite). That makes it a kite. Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 right angles. Its sides, in order, are 8 cm, 5 cm, 8 cm and 5 cm. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 right angles make it a rectangle. The sides are not all equal (8 cm and 5 cm), so it is not a square.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. Its diagonals meet at E. AC = 14 cm. How long is BD?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal, so BD = AC = 14 cm.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this rhombus. Which is true?
c: Neither one is cut in half
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles and cut each other in half. They are not equal: one is long and one is short.

items.q: Ayanda says the diagonals of every rhombus are equal in length. Is she right?
items.e: Equal sides do not mean equal diagonals. A rhombus that is not a square has one long and one short diagonal.

items.q: Which quadrilateral always has diagonals that are equal, cross at right angles and cut each other in half?
items.e: Equal diagonals come from being a rectangle, and right angles where they cross come from being a rhombus. Only a square is both.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this square. Which is true?
c: They are not equal in length
Equal, and cross at right angles
Neither one is cut in half
They do not cross at right angles
items.e: A square is a rectangle (equal diagonals) and a rhombus (diagonals at right angles). Its diagonals also cut each other in half.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. Its diagonals meet at E. What is the size of angle AEB?
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles, so angle AEB = 90°. (60° and 120° are angles of the rhombus itself.)

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this rhombus. Which is true?
c: Neither one is cut in half
They do not cross at right angles
They are not equal in length
items.e: The diagonals of this rhombus are different lengths. They do cross at right angles and cut each other in half. Only a square has equal diagonals among rhombuses.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this kite. Which is true?
c: They cut each other in half
items.e: The diagonals of a kite cross at right angles. The long diagonal cuts the short one in half, but not the other way round.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this trapezium. Which is true?
c: They cut each other in half
items.e: This trapezium has 2 equal sides (the slanted sides), so its diagonals are equal in length. They do not cut each other in half and do not cross at right angles.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this rectangle. Which is true?
c: Neither one is cut in half
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal in length and cut each other in half. They do not cross at right angles unless the rectangle is a square.

items.e: The angles of a triangle add to 180°. 50° + 60° = 110°, and 180° − 110° = 70°.

items.e: The small square is 90°. 180° − 90° − 38° = 52°. (142° forgets the right angle.)

items.e: The tick marks show an isosceles triangle, so the 2 bottom angles are equal: both are 70°. 180° − 70° − 70° = 40°.

items.q: Find the size of the angle marked “?”.
items.e: The tick marks show an isosceles triangle, so the 2 angles next to the unmarked side are equal. 180° − 50° = 130°, and 130° ÷ 2 = 65°.

items.e: 45° + 105° = 150°, and 180° − 150° = 30°. Turning the triangle does not change its angles.

items.q: Two angles of a triangle are 47° and 68°. What is the third angle?
A right triangle has one angle of 25°. What is the third angle?
items.e: The right angle is 90°. 180° − 90° − 25° = 65°. (155° forgets the right angle.)

items.q: Dumisani makes a stained-glass design from 4 congruent kites placed around a centre point, each one a quarter turn from the next. What is the order of rotational symmetry of the design?
items.e: Each quarter turn moves every kite onto the next one, so the design fits onto itself 4 times in a full turn: order 4.

items.q: Lerato draws a quadrilateral. All 4 sides are 5 cm. Its diagonals are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides make a rhombus. The diagonals are different lengths, so it is not a square. (Half-diagonals 3 cm and 4 cm make 5 cm sides.)

items.q: Priya sews 8 congruent rhombus patches for a quilt. Each side of one patch is 6 cm. How much ribbon does she need to go around all 8 patches?
items.e: One patch: 4 × 6 = 24 cm. The patches are congruent, so 8 patches need 8 × 24 = 192 cm.

items.q: Which statement is always true?
c: A rectangle’s diagonals cross at right angles
A square’s diagonals cross at right angles
A trapezium’s diagonals cut each other in half
items.e: A square is a rhombus, so its diagonals cross at right angles. The other statements are true only for some of those shapes.

items.q: A square cottage window has sides of 80 cm. Two wooden bars run along its diagonals. Each bar is about 113 cm long. About how far from a corner do the bars cross?
items.e: The diagonals of a square cut each other in half: 113 ÷ 2 = 56,5 cm. (40 cm is half a side, not half a diagonal.)

items.q: Sarah paints a sign shaped like a parallelogram. One angle is 70°. What is the size of an angle next to it?
items.e: Angles next to each other in a parallelogram add up to 180°: 180° − 70° = 110°. The angle opposite the 70° angle is also 70°.

items.q: Andile cuts a rectangular piece of cardboard, 30 cm by 20 cm, along one diagonal. What is true about the two pieces?
items.e: A diagonal cuts a rectangle into 2 triangles with sides 30 cm, 20 cm and the diagonal. A half turn puts one exactly on the other, so they are congruent.

items.q: Ethan measures a quadrilateral’s diagonals. Both are 10 cm, and they cut each other in half at right angles. What is it?
items.e: Equal diagonals that cut each other in half: rectangle. At right angles too: rhombus. Both: a square.

items.q: Dumisani’s family builds a garden bed with exactly one pair of parallel sides. The other two sides are equal. How many lines of symmetry does the garden bed have?
items.e: A trapezium with equal slanted sides has 1 line of symmetry, through the middles of the 2 parallel sides.

items.q: The short stick of Ravi’s kite is 60 cm long, and the long stick crosses it at its middle. How far is the crossing point from each end of the short stick?
items.e: The long diagonal cuts the short one in half: 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm.
